description:
pkix-aia/src/lib.rs documents AiaError::MalformedCertificate(String) as: 'Fetched bytes did not parse as a DER-encoded X.509 certificate. The inner `String` is an adapter-side diagnostic suitable for logging.' (lines 153-160). The variant's intent is to carry a parse-error description like 'expected SEQUENCE got SET' (per its own test at line 712).

In pkix-chain/src/lib.rs line 671-672, the chain-build slow path constructs:

    last_aia_error = Some(pkix_aia::AiaError::MalformedCertificate(uri.clone()));

…stuffing the URI into the diagnostic field instead of the parse error from <Certificate as der::Decode>::from_der(&der). The der::Error is discarded.

This is then encoded into the public test contract in tests/aia_chain_build.rs::aia_fetch_returns_garbage_surfaces_malformed_certificate (lines 286-288):

    pkix_chain::Error::Aia(AiaError::MalformedCertificate(uri)) => {
        assert_eq!(uri, "http://example.test/intermediate.der");
    }

…locking in the misuse.

CONSEQUENCES:
1. The variant's documented contract is violated. Adapters that return MalformedCertificate themselves (the pkix-aia docs even point at 'adapter-side diagnostic') will produce a value that means something different from what pkix-chain produces. A caller cannot disambiguate.
2. The actual root-cause der::Error is silently dropped. Debugging 'why did this CA's intermediate fail to parse' becomes impossible from the error alone — the user only knows WHICH URI failed (which they already provided), not WHY the bytes were bad.
3. The Display impl produces 'AIA-fetched bytes did not parse as a certificate: http://example.test/intermediate.der' which is nonsensical — the URI isn't the diagnostic.

FIX: Either (a) extend AiaError with a new variant like Aia(MalformedFetchedCertificate {uri, parse_error_display}); or (b) fix pkix-chain to put the actual der::Error.to_string() in the inner String and surface the URI separately (e.g. via the Error::Aia wrapper carrying a URI alongside the inner AiaError); or (c) document the field reuse and accept the per-adapter ambiguity. The current state — adapter docs say 'parse diagnostic', chain-build uses it as 'URI' — is incoherent.

The pkix-aia test at line 712 ('expected SEQUENCE got SET') and the pkix-chain test at line 287 ('http://example.test/intermediate.der') asserting DIFFERENT semantics on the same variant inner is the smoking gun.
title: AiaError::MalformedCertificate variant repurposed to carry URI instead of parse diagnostic
